## Findings
- claim-1: The lower-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) minimally generates \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 220-235]
- claim-2: If \(r=n-r\) and \(i=j\), the conjugate parameter \(v^\vee=v_{n-r,\;n-r+j-i,\;n-r-i+1,\;n}\) equals \(v\).
- claim-3: Under these hypotheses, partition conjugation induces a grading-preserving integral involution \(C:Q\to Q\), \(C([\bar s_\lambda])=[\bar s_{\lambda'}]\).
- claim-4: The involution \(C\) carries \(G_L\) bijectively onto \(G_R\).
## Strategy
The requested target is established, using the accepted quotient-conjugation route.

Put \(q=n-r=r\). Since \(i=j\),
\[
t=r-i+1,\qquad s=i+t-1=r.
\]
Hence
\[
v^\vee=v_{q,q+j-i,q-i+1,n}=v_{r,r,r-i+1,n}=v.
\]
The accepted quotient-conjugation isomorphism therefore specializes to a graded integral map
\[
C:Q=J_v/A_+J_v\longrightarrow Q,\qquad
C([\bar s_\lambda])=[\bar s_{\lambda'}].
\]
Because \((\lambda')'=\lambda\), \(C^2=\mathrm{id}_Q\); thus \(C\) is an involution.

Write
\[
G_L=\{\bar s_{(i^i,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq b^a\}.
\]
For \(\alpha=\rho'\subseteq a^b\),
\[
(i^i,\rho)'=(i+\alpha_1,\ldots,i+\alpha_b,i^{\,i-b}).
\]
As \(\rho\mapsto\rho'\) is bijective between partitions in \(b^a\) and those in \(a^b\), these are precisely the partitions \(\mu\) satisfying
\[
i^i\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{\,i-b}).
\]
Thus \(C\) carries \(G_L\) bijectively onto \(G_R\). This also includes \(a=0\).
